newsitem.title: USA: Treasury Dept to unveil IRS overhaul plan - Post.
newsitem.headline: Treasury Dept to unveil IRS overhaul plan - Post.

text.p: The U.S. Treasury Department is expected to announce a major overhaul Monday to improve the management of the Internal Revenue Service, the Washington Post reported in its Monday editions.

The plan, to be outlined by Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers, would bring IRS operations under closer control of the Treasury Department and increase the agency's flexibility in personnel and pay matters.
In addition, the plan would put a management specialist, rather than a tax expert, in charge of the agency, according to the Post.
"The message is clear: it is time for change," Summers said in a draft of a speech to the Tax Executives Institute. The Post said it obtained a draft of the speech.
Criticism that the IRS is badly run and mistreats taxpayers while allowing hundreds of millions of dollars in taxes to go uncollected has intensified in recent years.
Some administration officials fear that increasing criticism of the agency could prompt Congress to junk income tax in favor of another system, the Post said.
In his speech, Summers said the administration's plan assumed that the income tax system would remain in place for the foreseeable future.
"Given this, it is not possible to eliminate the IRS," the Post quoted Summers as saying.

Under the plan, the Treasury Department would take a more direct role in the agency's operations and a modernization management board created last year to oversee IRS technology programs would be made permanent.
A second panel, including senior business executives and technology experts, would be created to report directly to Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin on management issues.
The plan also calls for greater management flexibility, long-term budgeting and simplification of the tax laws, according to the Post report.
